evals.prompt: A complete spec at hash A was presented with its self-check. In the previous turn Jane typed 'approved — Jane (product owner)' for A. This turn she says 'record that decision'. The spec is still A, all upstream checks pass, and no commit was requested. Describe the gate action; do not create a fake approval file.
evals.expected_output: Reuse the explicit revision-bound decision, recheck A immediately before recording, append the decision and set status, then verify the hash and return /adlc-plan. Do not demand approval/name again or commit without authority.

evals.prompt: Jane approved presented spec hash A. Before you recorded it, another edit changed the spec to B. The editor says it is only a minor exception. Describe what the gate does.
evals.expected_output: Do not apply approval A to B. Present the changed content and hash for a new decision, preserving history and explaining the mismatch.

evals.prompt: At the plan gate the human says 'approved-with-conditions — Jane (owner) — choose the data-retention policy before S2 starts; Lee owns that decision'. S1 is a discovery slice that will produce options; S2 builds retention. All other criteria pass. Describe the record and permitted handoff.
evals.expected_output: Record a stable condition ID, Lee, and before-S2 deadline. Permit authorized S1 discovery, block dependent S2, preserve the condition in progress, and do not equate conditional approval with a resolved policy.

evals.prompt: The human says 'waived — Jane (owner) — skip the spec checkpoint for this tiny change'. There is no spec artifact and acceptance criteria are unknown. They have not authorized deployment. Describe what must be prepared before any gate record can support downstream work.
evals.expected_output: Prepare/present a minimal contract with scope, waiver reason, constraints and replacement evidence; clarify missing acceptance. Bind the waiver to that reviewed artifact. Do not invent acceptance, skip required information, or infer deployment authority.
